title: Urgent TTFT regression: adaptive batch-splitting hotfix for mixed-model serving
creator: Asha Menon
description: Summary: Several customers across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments reported sudden TTFT regressions (first-token latency) and reduced tokens/sec on steady-state streams for specific model families after the runtime kernel selector change shipped in runtime-2.3.0. Impact: high-latency spikes and throughput drops on multimodel endpoints (mix of quantized and full-precision variants) causing timeouts for interactive chat workloads and reduced SLA compliance for Dedicated tenants. Observed patterns: regressions most visible for models with short prompts and high concurrency, and for requests hitting cached KV entries followed by a cache miss. Goal: implement a targeted hotfix that restores TTFT and tokens/sec to pre-regression baseline without risking instability in other workloads.
steps_to_repro: Deploy runtime-2.3.0 or later with new kernel selector enabled
Create a multimodel route that routes small-chat requests to quantized-variant by policy
Open 50 concurrent short prompt websocket streams (avg prompt length 12 tokens) per GPU slot
Measure TTFT distribution and tokens/sec over 5 minutes; observe 2-6x TTFT increase on first token and 20-40% throughput drop across affected models
summary_of_root_cause: A regression in kernel selection heuristics combined with an aggressive batching decision allowed some requests to be assigned to larger micro-batches when their KV cache had partial validity, increasing setup time for first token. Additionally, a new continuous-batching path introduced suboptimal CUDA kernel shapes for short-sequence workloads on specific quantized kernels, degrading tokens/sec.
mitigation_actions: Immediate: Rollback heuristic flag for kernel-selector to previous stable value on hosted control plane (rolled at 2026-03-10 02:30 UTC)
Emergency config: Set dynamic_batch.max_microbatch_size=8 for Dedicated pools with short-sequence traffic patterns
Hotfix patch: Implement adaptive batch-splitting that detects KV-cache hot-paths and forces single-request dispatch for TTFT-sensitive requests
Traffic steering: Apply temporary routing to keep interactive small-prompt workload on earlier quantized-variant (variant-v1) where available
